title: Prove D(n) = round(n!/e) for n≥2 as integer identity

problemStatement.formal: theorem derangements_round_eq (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) : (Nat.numDerangements n : ℤ) = Int.round (↑(n !) / Real.exp 1)
problemStatement.plain: The number of derangements of n elements equals the nearest integer to n!/e, for n ≥ 2. This is an integer identity following from the sharp error bound |D(n)/n! - e⁻¹| ≤ 1/(n+1)! already proved in the gallery.
whyMatters: Bridges the real-valued convergence theorem to a computationally useful integer formula
Demonstrates the practical power of the sharp error bound 1/(n+1)! < 1/2 for n ≥ 1
Template for 'nearest-integer' identities involving transcendental constants
Direct extension of gallery proof requiring only API assembly in Lean

open: Lean 4 formalization connecting real-valued bound to Int.round
knownResults.goal: Prove (Nat.numDerangements n : ℤ) = Int.round (↑(n !) / Real.exp 1) for n ≥ 2

currentState.focus: Initial problem understanding. Read problem.md and gather context.
